chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman and then learned after marrying her that she had committed fornication. He said: 'If her husband wishes, he may take the dowry from the one who married her off to him, and she is entitled to the dowry for having made her private part permissible to him; and if he wishes, he may leave her (without divorcing or returning the dowry).'

key_terms.تَرَكَهَا: He left her (kept her without divorce)

ai.seo_question: What are the husband's rights regarding dowry if his wife committed fornication before marriage?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the financial and marital rights when a wife’s pre-marital fornication is discovered, emphasizing the husband's discretion to either retain the wife with full dowry rights or seek compensation from her guardian. This ruling highlights the concept of *khiyarat* (options) in marriage contracts, allowing the husband to decide based on whether he prefers the financial restitution or the continuation of the marital bond. The narration underscores the importance of transparency in marital contracts and the specific legal standing of the *wali* in guaranteeing the bride's status.
